definitions.gloss: before one's very eyes, firsthand, in person
definitions.explanation: Witnessing something directly and personally rather than hearing about it secondhand. Almost always used in the form {目|ま}の{当|あ}たりにする (to witness firsthand).

examples.japanese: {事故|じこ}を{目|ま}の{当|あ}たりにした。
{被害|ひがい}の{大|おお}きさを{目|ま}の{当|あ}たりにして{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: I was shocked when I saw the extent of the damage firsthand.

examples.japanese: {自然|しぜん}の{壮大|そうだい}さを{目|ま}の{当|あ}たりにすると、{人間|にんげん}の{小|ちい}ささを{感|かん}じる。
examples.english: When you witness the grandeur of nature firsthand, you feel how small humans are.

notes:
USAGE:
Almost exclusively used in the fixed pattern {目|ま}の{当|あ}たりにする (to witness, to see with one's own eyes). Carries a strong nuance of personal, direct experience — often of something surprising, shocking, or impressive.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {目|ま}の{当|あ}たりにする: to witness firsthand
- {現実|げんじつ}を{目|ま}の{当|あ}たりにする: to see reality firsthand
- {惨状|さんじょう}を{目|ま}の{当|あ}たりにする: to witness a terrible scene firsthand
